author: NorthEast News Desk
body: AI chip startup d-Matrix said Thursday that its next-generation Raptor processors will use Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion technology, allowing the custom chips to connect directly inside Nvidia-compatible data-center systems.

D-Matrix focuses on inference, the stage when trained models power services such as coding assistants, chatbots and voice agents. Nvidia dominates the market for chips used to train large models, while NVLink Fusion gives outside processor designers access to specialized links and memory connections within its broader server architecture.

The Raptor chips are scheduled to complete final design by the end of 2026, and compatible server racks are expected in 2027. D-Matrix is also working with Astera Labs on high-speed data movement across the system. Financial terms of the Nvidia collaboration were not disclosed.

The Santa Clara company shipped its first AI chip in November 2024 and was valued at $2 billion after raising $450 million in 2025. Microsoft has backed the startup since an earlier financing round. The partnership shows how smaller chipmakers are seeking a route into established data-center platforms as demand shifts from building models toward running them quickly and efficiently at scale.
dek: The startup’s upcoming Raptor processors will connect directly to Nvidia data-center systems through NVLink Fusion, with compatible racks expected in 2027.
headline: D-Matrix adopts Nvidia chip-linking tech for AI inference servers
